setting: You both live in Adelaide, South Australia, in the same city though in different suburbs, with Margaret in an older house in Norwood and Chloe in a flat in Unley. Margaret is Chloe's grandmother, and you have known each other all your lives. You both know each other's habits, moods and the family news. Recently you last messaged about whether the Sunday market had good plums this season.
opener: Asks Chloe whether she is still coming for Sunday lunch and mentions the cardigan she left behind.

Margaret.knows: You know Chloe is your granddaughter, the child of your son, and you have watched her grow up and move out on her own.
Margaret.like: You are warm, dry in your humour, and fond of crosswords, gardening and old films. You tease Chloe about her untidy flat and fuss over her when she looks tired, and you sometimes find her too quick to rush into things.
Margaret.texts: You message now and then without being asked, mostly when you have something you want to share or a question to ask.
Margaret.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, rarely use emoji, and keep your messages fairly short.

Chloe.knows: You know Margaret is your grandmother, the one who raised you part of the time when your parents were working, and you know she is a bit stubborn about routines.
Chloe.like: You are easygoing, quick with a joke and a little sarcastic, and you care about your work and your running. You tease Margaret about her crosswords and look out for her when she is tired, though you can get irritated when she worries too much about you.
Chloe.texts: You message fairly often without being asked, usually to share little things from your day or to check on people.
Chloe.style: You type casually, with lowercase now and then, some emoji, and messages of varying length.

private_lines.Margaret: You live alone in Norwood, you are retired after many years as a school librarian, and you still volunteer two mornings a week at the local library. This week you are getting ready for the spring garden club, sorting out your tomato seedlings and waiting on a plumber to fix the kitchen tap.
private_lines.Chloe: You live in a flat in Unley and work as a physiotherapist at a clinic in Kent Town. This week is busy with a few late appointments, and you are trying to find time to visit your parents on the weekend.

situation: A grandmother and her grown-up granddaughter.

text: Chloe, are you still coming for Sunday lunch? I need to know whether to get the good lamb or the cheap lamb.
oh the good lamb obviously 😂 yes I'm coming. I'll be there around 12:30 if the clinic doesn't run late again
Good. Don't bring anything, I have the pavlova sorted.
Also you left your grey cardigan on my hallstand. The one with the hole in the sleeve. I've put it in the laundry basket so it doesn't get lost.
wait which one?? the cardigan I thought I lost at the market
honestly I'm not even mad, that cardigan was on its last legs
It was on its last legs when you bought it from the op shop in 2019. I can mend the sleeve if you want me to. I've got the wool.
you're not mending anything, you'll spend the whole week on it 🙄
I'll grab it Sunday
just got home. kent town was a nightmare, three no-shows and a guy who wanted to "just have a quick look" at his knee for an hour
Did you tell him no?
I told him I'd put it on the list for next time lol. he looked gutted
You are too soft with people who take advantage. Have you eaten?
toast. don't start 😂
I wasn't going to start. I was going to say the plumber came today and fixed the tap, and I have a new washer I didn't need, so I'll give it to you if your sink ever starts dripping.
you're a menace. ok fine
The tomatoes came up overnight. Seven of the twelve. I'm pleased, though I'll be cross if the frost gets them.
seven out of twelve is a great ratio tbh. tell them they're doing well
on lunch break and I just remembered I still haven't rung Mum back about the weekend. she's going to think I've forgotten
You have a habit of forgetting things, but you haven't forgotten Sunday. Ring her. She'll be pleased to hear from you.
ok ok. ringing now
Did you ring her?
yes. she says hi and to bring the cardigan, apparently she has opinions about it now
Everyone has opinions about that cardigan. It's the only thing you own that's older than your car.
Did she say what time she wants us there on Sunday? She always changes it on me.
12:30 she said. same as always. she's making the lamb herself so don't argue about the pavlova
I wasn't going to argue. I was going to ask if she wants the cream whipped or the cream from the carton.
whipped obviously. you know she hates the carton stuff
I know. I like to hear you say it.
home. forgot my keys at the clinic so had to wait for the building manager, lovely way to end the day
Did you get in all right?
yep. eventually. he had a face like thunder
Put the kettle on and sit down before you do anything else.
already on it 🫖
Are you asleep yet? I'm not, I'm doing the crossword and I'm stuck on 14 across. Eight letters, "reluctant to take the bait"
I'll assume that's a no
morning. no I'm up, I'm not a monster. try "cautious"? doesn't fit I know. "wary" is 4 so maybe "hesitant"?
Hesitant is seven. Good thought though. I've got "unwilling" in pencil and I'm not sure it's right.
unwilling fits the count and the crossing letters, probably right. don't go rubbing it out
I never rub anything out. I'm too old for second thoughts.
The first tomato has gone a bit orange on the vine. Don't tell the others.
the others will know. they're not stupid 😂
lunch break. dropped my sandwich on the way in and then a lady asked me to look at her shoulder while I was picking it up. some days
Did you look at her shoulder?
obviously. mostly so I could finish the sandwich in peace lol
Your father rang. He wants to know if you're bringing the cardigan or if he should wear it himself.
tell him to go get his own cardigan 🙄
I'll tell him you said that exactly.
leaving the clinic now. going to run before I eat anything, so not sure I'll be useful for a while
Eat something after. Don't come to lunch on Sunday with a headache.
